summary: This case study details the integration and maintainer review process for a read-only external proof verification tool within the OTSkit-MCP repository. The author documents the architectural boundaries, mutation controls, feature-gate compliance, and size-bound checks required to safely land the feature in v0.9.0. Overall, it provides solid, reproducible real-world engineering insights for agent-facing cryptographic utilities.
strengths: Clear, highly reproducible real-world engineering documentation backed by a public open-source repository and specific commit hashes.
Thoughtful security and boundary considerations, including local-first mutation testing, feature gating, and file size capping.
Well-structured narrative outlining the problem, design boundaries, testing methodology, and reviewer feedback loop.
weaknesses: Case study scope is narrow and specific to a niche protocol integration, limiting broad generalizability.
Discussion of negative claims and limitations, while valuable, could be expanded to explore broader failure modes in agent-facing tooling.
suggestions: Include a short code snippet or architectural diagram showing how the feature gate interacts with the verification tool call.
Elaborate slightly on how other MCP servers might adopt similar read-only, bounded verification patterns.

claims.text: The resulting work became OTSkit-MCP pull request #41, merged on 2026-09-06 and released as @otskit/mcp v0.9.0.
The new tool was not included in the server's existing stamp feature gate, so an operator who disabled stamping could still invoke it.

novelty_vs_existing.title: Fail-closed transactional macOS updater with a separate rollback key, locally proven and cryptographically disabled in the public tree
novelty_vs_existing.contribution: Documents protocol verification boundaries for agent tooling rather than OS-level transactional updaters.
